rules.surface_condition: cuts that split a numeral from its unit/quantified noun (number on the left, measurement/unit or counted-noun on the right)
rules.blamed_rule: - Left or right stretch that ends or begins with a lexical token translators typically render reliably will tend to raise the measured value. Examples of such surface forms: numerals and formatted numbers (e.g., "1,200", "2050"), explicit dates, percentages, currency figures, and short fixed named phrases (e.g., organization names, place names). (Prediction to test: cuts adjacent to numerals/dates often score high.)
rules.proposed_rule: Scoring Rules: If the token immediately before the marker is a NUM and the token immediately after the marker is a measurement unit or counted-noun (see list), treat this boundary as risky and move its score well down (target band 10–35) rather than giving an upward bias. Rationale: the model's current numeral-first heuristic boosts such cuts, but splitting a numeral from its unit or the noun it quantifies frequently produces contradiction or misrendering.

rules.surface_condition: cuts that split coordinated/ranged numerals or ordinals (a number/ordinal on the left, immediately followed by 'and' or 'or' on the right)
rules.blamed_rule: - Cuts before or after subordinators or coordinators can measure well when the segment to the left or right is itself translated reliably (e.g., if the left already ends in a named entity or numeral). Example surface words: "and", "but", "however", "when", "after", "since", "while", "which", "that", "who". Do not assume these always help; the testable prediction is only that presence of reliable lexical material on one side increases measured score.
rules.proposed_rule: Scoring Rules: If the token immediately before the marker is a NUM or common ordinal (first, second, third, ... tenth) and the token immediately after the marker is 'and' or 'or', do not apply the usual upward bias for numerals; instead lower the score into a conservative band (target band 5–30). Rationale: splitting coordinated numeric ranges/ordinals ("between the second | and fourth", "2015 | or 2016") frequently severs a single quantified/paired expression and yields high contradiction or low reliability.

tie_fix: Ties arise when multiple markers land in the same surface bucket (e.g., several adjacent markers are all 'near a numeral' or 'near a comma') and receive identical heuristic boosts. Fix: deterministically break same-bucket ties by a small position-based offset (earlier marker loses a fixed tiny rank bump) or by token-class priority (units < ordinals < plain NUM) so the model never emits identical integers.
summary: The prompt currently over-weights numerals and adjacent coordinators: it boosts any cut next to a number (or ordinal) even when that number is part of a multiword measurement or a coordinated range. That produces many over-trust errors where splitting the numeral from its unit or from the rest of a paired expression yields high contradiction or poor measured fidelity. The two proposed rules consistently lower scores for (a) numeral↔unit splits and (b) numeral/ordinal↔(and|or) splits, returning those boundaries to more conservative bands so the kept set better matches measured quality.
